claims.text: GPT-4 achieves 98% accuracy in Experiment 1A and 96% accuracy in Experiment 1B when selecting human-preferred scope readings.
Llama 2 70B achieves 88% accuracy in Experiment 1A and 89% accuracy in Experiment 1B when selecting human-preferred scope readings.
GPT-3.5-text-davinci-003 achieves 91% accuracy in Experiment 1A and 87% accuracy in Experiment 1B on selecting human-preferred scope readings.
Smaller language models such as Llama 2 7B and GPT-3 davinci perform near chance level (58% accuracy) on scope disambiguation Q&A tasks.
Removing the ambiguous sentence from the prompt in the control setting causes accuracy to drop significantly for advanced models like GPT-4 (from 98% to 75% in Experiment 1A).
Language models generally exhibit lower accuracy on sentences with a preferred inverse scope reading than on those with a preferred surface scope reading.
Larger autoregressive language models assign log-probability ratios to follow-ups that indicate sensitivity to scope ambiguity in sentences.
Model ambiguity recognition scores (alpha-scores) correlate positively with human naturalness judgments, reaching a Pearson correlation of R=0.62 for text-davinci-003 in Experiment 2A.
Large language models perform poorly when evaluated on scope ambiguity via explicit True/False meta-linguistic prompts, achieving 64% accuracy or lower.

evidence.description: GPT-4 achieved 0.98 accuracy in Experiment 1A test setting (Table 3) and 0.96 accuracy in Experiment 1B test setting (Table 5).
Llama2-70b achieved 0.88 accuracy in Experiment 1A (Table 3) and 0.89 accuracy in Experiment 1B (Table 5).
GPT-3.5-td003 achieved 0.91 accuracy in Experiment 1A (Table 3) and 0.87 accuracy in Experiment 1B (Table 5).
Llama2-7b got 0.58 accuracy in Exp 1A test and 0.67 in control; GPT-3-davinci scored 0.58 accuracy in both test and control settings (Table 3).
In Table 3, GPT-4 test accuracy was 0.98 vs 0.75 in control; in Table 5, GPT-4 test accuracy was 0.96 vs 0.72 in control.
In Exp 1A, Llama2-70b-chat achieved 0.88 surface accuracy vs 0.78 inverse accuracy; GPT-3.5-turbo scored 0.81 surface vs 0.77 inverse accuracy (Table 3).
All models except GPT-2-small produced statistically significant positive mean alpha-scores in Exp 2A (Table 4) and Exp 2B (Table 6).
text-davinci-003 obtained a Pearson correlation R=0.62 (p=2.93e-04) with human proxy scores in Exp 2A (Table 4) and R=0.48 (p=1.09e-07) in Exp 2B (Table 6).
When adapting the dataset to Liu et al. (2023)'s True/False format, GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-turbo achieved 0.64 accuracy, while Llama 2 models ranged between 0.44 and 0.59 (Table 7).

methodologies.name: Quantifier Scope Disambiguation Q&A Method
methodologies.description: Presents models with scope-ambiguous sentences alongside Option A and Option B choices corresponding to surface and inverse scope interpretations, evaluating selection accuracy against human majority preferences in test and prompt-omitted control settings.
datasets: LSAT quantifier scope dataset (AnderBois et al., 2012)
Original Scope Ambiguity Dataset 1A (153 unique sentences)
Expanded Scope Ambiguity Dataset 1B (837 unique sentences)

methodologies.name: Continuation Log-Probability Ambiguity Recognition (Alpha-Score)
methodologies.description: Measures model log-probabilities of surface-compatible and inverse-compatible follow-up sentences following an ambiguous sentence S versus an unambiguous control sentence Sc, calculating an alpha-score to quantify sensitivity to meaning ambiguity.
datasets: Handcrafted Scope Ambiguity Dataset 2A (29 unique datapoints)
Expanded Scope Ambiguity Dataset 2B (110 unique datapoints)
conditions: ambiguous sentence S vs unambiguous control Sc
inverse follow-up F1 vs surface follow-up F2

methodologies.name: Meta-linguistic True/False Prompting Evaluation
methodologies.description: Prompts models to explicitly evaluate True/False statements regarding whether an ambiguous sentence can or cannot mean a specified disambiguation.
datasets: Subset of Expanded Scope Ambiguity Dataset 2B
conditions: True/False prompt format from Liu et al. (2023)

limitations.text: The study focuses exclusively on English scope ambiguities.
The experiments do not assess how explicit background discourse contexts affect scope reading preferences.
The behavioral evaluation does not reveal how or where internal model weights represent scope structures.
Prior datasets evaluating LLM scope ambiguity were limited in scale, lacked stimulus diversity, or contained very few scope ambiguity instances.

future_work.text: Investigating how background discourse contexts influence LLM scope reading preferences.
Applying parallel model interpretability methods, such as causal mediation analysis, to determine where and how LLMs internally represent scope.
